recipes.name: Horizontal application layout
recipes.purpose: Layout with horizontal navigation above the main content area. The most common way of displaying the top-level pages of a site. Source: design.visa.com › Application layouts › Usage › Navigational frames.
guidance: Sizes in the kit: 768, 1024, 1280, 1440, 1600 Fixed, 1600 Fluid (Size variant). Source: kit, set Horizontal.

Grid for horizontal layouts: 375 = 4 columns, margins 16, gutters 16; 768 to 1023 = 8 columns, margins 16, gutters 24; 1024 to 1600+ = 12 columns, margins 24, gutters 24; 1600+ fixed = 12 columns, margins 80 minimum, gutters 24. Source: design.visa.com › Responsive grid system › Breakpoints.

Fluid grids scale with the screen width (dashboards, data-heavy designs); fixed grids keep a maximum width and grow the margins (text-heavy designs). Source: design.visa.com › Responsive grid system › Fixed vs. fluid grids.

Establish a clear visual hierarchy when using more than one level of navigation. Do not rearrange or mix the pre-built layouts against common UX conventions. Source: design.visa.com › Application layouts › Usage › Do and Don't.
anatomy: Horizontal (horizontal navigation, 80 high, app name left, navigation right)
Content area base (full width under the navigation)
Default footer (64 high, at the bottom)
Flag: Success (hidden; top right of the content, Show flag)
Dialog with overlay (hidden; centered, Show dialog)
examples: Form page: Form title, description, Section message, fields, Submit / Save / Cancel (the content the kit shows inside Content area base)

recipes.name: Stacked horizontal application layout
recipes.purpose: Layout with a secondary navigation bar under the primary horizontal bar, for applications with a larger number of main navigation items. Source: design.visa.com › Application layouts › Usage › Navigational frames.
guidance: Sizes in the kit: 1024, 1280, 1440, 1600 Fixed, 1600 Fluid. Source: kit, set Horizontal stacked.
Same grid as the horizontal layouts. Source: design.visa.com › Responsive grid system › Horizontal and advanced layouts.
anatomy: Stacked horizontal (Horizontal on top, Secondary nav with a horizontal Tab Group under it, bottom border; 149 high)
Content area base
Default footer
Flag: Success (hidden)
Dialog with overlay (hidden)
examples: Form page under a two-level navigation

recipes.name: Vertical application layout
recipes.purpose: Layout with vertical navigation beside the main content area, for a large number of navigation items or when horizontal space is limited. Source: design.visa.com › Application layouts › Usage › Navigational frames.
guidance: Sizes in the kit: 1024, 1280, 1440, 1600. Source: kit, set Vertical.
The collapsed variant (set Vertical-Collapsed) replaces the drawer by a 42 wide rail with one UI icon at the bottom; the content area takes the rest. Source: kit.

Grid for vertical and mixed layouts: begins to the right of the navigation; 12 columns at every size; margins 24 at 1024 to 1279 and 32 from 1280 up; gutters 24. Fixed in Figma, can be built fluid. Source: design.visa.com › Responsive grid system › Vertical and mixed layouts.
anatomy: Vertical nav default (242 wide, full height: App name, Nav Items, Bottom items)
Content area + footer beside it: Content area base over Default footer
Flag: Success (hidden)

examples: Form page beside a vertical navigation with five L1 items and a user row at the bottom

recipes.name: Mixed application layout
recipes.purpose: Horizontal and vertical navigation combined, for complex applications: the horizontal bar holds global items, the vertical panel holds local items. Source: design.visa.com › Application layouts › Usage › Navigational frames.
guidance: Sizes in the kit: 1024, 1280, 1440, 1600. Collapsed variant: set Mixed-Collapsed (42 wide rail). Source: kit.
Same grid as the vertical layouts. Source: design.visa.com › Responsive grid system › Vertical and mixed layouts.
anatomy: Horizontal (80 high, on top)
Vertical nav default (242 wide) under it, at the left
Content area + footer beside the vertical nav: Content area base over Default footer
Flag: Success (hidden)
Dialog with overlay (hidden)
examples: Form page with global L1 items on top and local L2 items at the left

recipes.name: Content area
recipes.purpose: The primary section of the interface where the main information, features and interactive elements are displayed. Can span several columns; information in a logical order along the user flow. Source: design.visa.com › Application layouts › Usage › Content areas.
guidance: Content areas reflow at every breakpoint; define reflow as percentages or column spans (6 columns at 1600 may become 4 at 1280). Source: design.visa.com › Responsive grid system › Content reflow.
Vertical spacing in factors of four: 16, 24, 32, 48. Avoid half pixels and odd numbers. Source: design.visa.com › Responsive grid system › System baseline.

Web components have a base height of 38; the mobile scale is 1.25 times larger, base height 46. Body 2 is the base body size: 14 on web, 16 on mobile. Source: design.visa.com › Responsive grid system › Component size, Typography size.
anatomy: Margins: white space along the edges
Content area: the space left once margins are defined

Kit examples inside Content area base: type ramp (Overline, Headline 1 to 4, Subtitle 1 to 3, Body), Dialog: Default, Banner, Panel (Responsive panel title), Form layout (Form title, description, Section message, fields, Submit / Save / Cancel)

recipes.name: Mobile application layout
recipes.purpose: The same application pages at 375 wide: a Top app bar, the content area, and the mobile footer or tab bar. 375 is the reference width; design responsively. Source: kit, section Mobile application layouts; design.visa.com › Application layouts › Usage › Platform considerations.
guidance: Mobile grid: 4 columns, margins 16, gutters 16 at 375. Tablet reference width 768: 8 columns, margins 16, gutters 24. Source: design.visa.com › Responsive grid system › Breakpoints.
Mobile components are 1.25 times the web scale (Platform mode Mobile in the variables). Source: design.visa.com › Responsive grid system › Component size; kit variables, collection Platform.
